tools.name: publish
tools.description:
Publish files as a live website on Flowershow and get a shareable URL. Use when the user says "publish this", "put this online", "make this a website", "share this as a page" or "host this".

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "publish" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Publish files as a live website on Flowershow and get a shareable URL. Use when the user says "publish this", "put this online", "make this a website", "share t…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "publish" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: publish · Private data: publish · Public sink: publish · Destructive: publish.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: publish · Private data: publish · Public sink: publish · Destructive: publish

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
